title: Automated High-Throughput Correlated Electron and Light Microscopy of Semiconductor Nanowires
content: Semiconducting nanowires made of III–V materials, are of considerable interest in the field of nanotechnology due to their unique properties, such as high surface-area-to-volume ratio, low defect density, and direct bandgaps [1] making them suitable for a variety of (opto)electronic applications. Indium Arsenide (InAs) nanowires, in particular, are notable for their high carrier mobility and effective spin transport capabilities, motivating their integration into devices. Bottom-up growth techniques, such as metal organic chemical vapour deposition (MOCVD) allow for control over the nanowires’ physical geometry, composition and intrinsic properties, but scaling up nanowire-based devices is challenging due to the inherent inhomogeneity in nanowire deposition.
